title: In vitro degradation and biocompatibility evaluation of typical biodegradable metals (Mg/Zn/Fe) for the application of tracheobronchial stenosis

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: A biodegradable metal stent for tracheobronchial stenosis needs a suitable degradation rate in airway fluid and compatibility with airway epithelium. Compare three typical biodegradable metals: high-purity Mg, high-purity Zn and pure Fe.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/need), s2 (DES/base_system), s3 (DES/variable_sweep), s4 (DES/method), s5 (PRC/stimulus), s6 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: HP-Mg is attacked over its whole surface (SBF by 7 d, GS by 14 d), while HP-Zn and P-Fe show only local attack. Corrosion products on all three metals in both media are carbonates and phosphates

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: In GS, less chloride and adsorbed mucin and bicarbonate keep the protective product film intact, which slows corrosion. HP-Mg degrades about an order of magnitude faster than HP-Zn and P-Fe in both media.
states.detail: Absorbed: s9 (MEC/pathway), s10 (PRP/value), s11 (PRP/value), s12 (PRP/value), s13 (MEC/pathway). Premises: SBF contains about 1.3x the chloride and 7.3x the bicarbonate of GS; GS contains 0.6 g/L protein; Chloride breaks down protective films and causes pitting; bicarbonate and adsorbed protein build insoluble protective layers; Fe-based stents stimulated proliferation of L929 and ECV304 cells in an earlier study

states.title: Performance state
states.head: For airway stents HP-Zn combines slow degradation with good epithelial compatibility; HP-Mg degrades fast, P-Fe is cytotoxic

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: In airway-simulating in-vitro tests, HP-Mg and HP-Zn outperform P-Fe for cell compatibility, and the GS medium makes all metals degrade more slowly than SBF

nodes.title: SEM, F2
nodes.head: SEM: HP-Mg surface pitted in GS and fully roughened in SBF; HP-Zn and P-Fe mostly smooth with local attack
nodes.solves: HP-Mg is attacked over its whole surface (SBF by 7 d, GS by 14 d), while HP-Zn and P-Fe show only local attack
nodes.note: HP-Zn in SBF at 14 d (F2b D) shows dense dark flakes over much of the field, more than the "discrete sites" stated

nodes.title: MICRO, F5
nodes.head: Fluorescence: P-Fe wells nearly empty in IC at days 2 and 4 and sparse in EC at day 4, while HP-Mg and HP-Zn EC wells are confluent
nodes.solves: HP-Mg and HP-Zn support A549 attachment and proliferation, while P-Fe lowers cell density and viability
nodes.necessity_reason: s12 keeps shown support from b13 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F1, F3
nodes.head: HP-Mg: icorr about 18 uA/cm2 in SBF vs about 1.5 in GS; Ecorr -1.76 vs -1.52 V(SCE). 28 d rates: HP-Mg 0.78 (GS) vs 2.0 mm/y (SBF); HP-Zn about 0.03 vs 0.10; P-Fe about 0.10 vs 0.13.
nodes.solves: Degradation is slower in GS than in SBF, most strongly for HP-Mg (28 d: 0.78 vs 2.0 mm/y)
nodes.note: HP-Zn icorr also visibly higher in SBF (~5.6) than GS (~1.7), although text reports no significant difference for HP-Zn
nodes.detail: b1: HP-Mg: icorr about 18 uA/cm2 in SBF vs about 1.5 in GS; Ecorr -1.76 vs -1.52 V(SCE); b7: 28 d rates: HP-Mg 0.78 (GS) vs 2.0 mm/y (SBF); HP-Zn about 0.03 vs 0.10; P-Fe about 0.10 vs 0.13; b8: HP-Mg rate in GS rises steadily from 0.13 to 0.78 mm/y over 7-28 d while in SBF it falls from 3.4 to 2.0, so the gap narrows from ~25x to ~2.6x
nodes.inner_audit: b8: HP-Mg rate in GS rises steadily from 0.13 to 0.78 mm/y over 7-28 d while in SBF it falls from 3.4 to 2.0, so the gap narrows from ~25x to ~2.6x

nodes.title: ASSAY, EDS:spectrum, F1, F3, F4
nodes.head: Polarisation curves: Ecorr about -0.70/-0.77 (P-Fe), -1.21/-1.27 (HP-Zn), -1.52/-1.76 V (HP-Mg) in GS/SBF. EDS: P + Ca about 25 at% on HP-Mg in SBF vs about 2-3 at% in GS; HP-Zn about 24 vs 6 at%; base metal share much higher in GS.
nodes.note: judge: HP-Zn SBF stack reads Ca ~16 + P ~8.5 at% (earlier label gave 16 for P+Ca); P-Fe P+Ca ~9 (GS) vs ~4 at% (SBF), opposite direction, text silent
nodes.detail: b2: Polarisation curves: Ecorr about -0.70/-0.77 (P-Fe), -1.21/-1.27 (HP-Zn), -1.52/-1.76 V (HP-Mg) in GS/SBF; b4: EDS: P + Ca about 25 at% on HP-Mg in SBF vs about 2-3 at% in GS; HP-Zn about 24 vs 6 at%; base metal share much higher in GS; b9: pH in GS starts at 8.0-8.4, falls below SBF after about 10-13 d and fluctuates to 6.8-7.1; SBF stays mostly 7.1-7.5 (HP-Mg SBF ~7.8-8.0 in the first 2 d, P-Fe SBF dips to 6.9)
nodes.necessity_reason: s11, s9 keeps shown support from b1, b7, b8 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: CCK-8: P-Fe-IC stays about 0.4-0.5 at days 3 and 5 vs negative control 1.9 and 2.6; by day 5 HP-Mg-IC, HP-Zn-IC and HP-Mg-EC reach or exceed the control, other Mg/Zn groups 1.8-2.3
nodes.solves: HP-Mg and HP-Zn support A549 attachment and proliferation, while P-Fe lowers cell density and viability
nodes.note: at day 1 all groups lie within 0.45-0.75 and P-Fe-IC (~0.45) equals the negative control (~0.47), so the text claim that P-Fe-IC was most cytotoxic versus the negative group at day 1 is not visible; P-Fe-EC is highest at day 3 (~2.8) and drops to ~0.9 at day 5
